nodes.description: Root node representing the patient whose longitudinal clinical data is being tracked.
History and detailed log of individual panic attacks, including triggers, symptoms, context, duration, and patient responses.
Patterns and trends in mood ratings (anxiety, depression, worry) over time.
Known and suspected triggers or antecedent events for panic/anxiety episodes.
Clusters of symptoms experienced during panic attacks or periods of anxiety.
Taxonomy and patterns of negative thoughts, including themes, cognitive errors, catastrophic beliefs, and changes over time.
Patterns of avoidance, situations most frequently avoided, safety behaviors, and reliance on maladaptive coping strategies.
Coping strategies during and after panic attacks, including application and efficacy of CBT skills.
Relevant contextual factors such as time, place, presence of others, and environmental stresses during anxiety/panic episodes.
Documented beliefs about anxiety, panic, dangerousness of symptoms, and cognitive appraisals (including enduring myths, catastrophic beliefs, and changes over time).
Individualized ranking of feared situations or activities, with subjective anxiety ratings and exposure progression.
Progress across the exposure hierarchy, details of exposure tasks (triggers, duration, anxiety levels), and associated learning.
Completion, compliance, barriers, outcome, and engagement with assigned homework and practice exercises.
Patient’s evolving insight and metacognitive understanding of CBT concepts, therapeutic rationale, and disorder.
List of significant others involved, nature of relationships, roles in exposure sessions, communication strategies, and reinforcement patterns.
Types, dosages, response, side effects, withdrawal experiences, and response during titration or cessation.
History and monitoring of medical conditions and contraindications (e.g., for breathing exercises) that may affect therapy.
Patient’s long-term life goals, therapy milestones, setbacks, and progress towards those goals.
